fields: Identity CpG site-selection rule (the criteria that define a cell type's identity sites for Met-A)

A chain rule — not part of IAM's Law — that sets which CpG sites count as a cell type's identity sites for Met-A: a site qualifies only if its healthy spread is <= 0.05, its mean methylation falls in the range 0.75-0.95 or in the range 0.05-0.25, and no more than 3,000 such sites are kept per side.
Filters the candidate CpG sites down to the set Met-A treats as a cell type's identity sites, using the spread, mean-level, and per-side count thresholds given in the rule.

Met-A's job is to read the healthy height of each cell's identity sites and test whether a type's level is physics or a quirk of IAM-A; it needs a fixed rule for which sites count as 'identity sites' before that height can be measured consistently, which is what this rule (plain: 'which sites Met-A reads') provides.
How it is obtained or computed

fields: Normal range (reference interval) for Met-A scores; under the agreed rule, each reading expressed as its distance from 1 in units of the cell type's measured healthy width

The yardstick a Met-A entropy reading is judged against. The agreed rule is that there is no fixed plus-or-minus band — '1 is in the middle,' and each reading is recorded as its distance from 1 in units of that cell type's own measured healthy width. What currently sits in the code instead is '0.95-1.05,' a holdover from the old cell-class h_min method, explicitly marked as not the agreed method.

It is meant to turn a raw Met-A entropy score into a judgment of whether a reading sits at each cell type's own healthy level or outside it, expressed as a distance from 1 in units of a measured healthy width rather than a flat percentage band.

Met-A's job is to test whether a cell type's healthy entropy level is physics or a quirk of IAM-A, and the agreed note states plainly there is no reason to impose a plus-or-minus-5-percent band on anything — the instrument needs a range measured from real atlas donors (and confirmed on outside healthy people) so that an off-centre type can be explained rather than hidden inside an arbitrary band.
How it is obtained or computed

Per the agreed rule: measured as the atlas's own donors read against the atlas (held out), then confirmed on outside healthy people; each reading is recorded as its distance from 1 in units of that measured width, and even '1 is the middle' is itself tested rather than assumed. Source: stage_metaa_atlas.RULE.normal; source_kind: setting with a default (a chain rule).

fields: Healthy width by cell (the agreed band method)
Per-cell-type healthy reference interval for the Met-A score (donor-based prediction interval around 1)

The agreed method (2026-11-07: no fixed band, 1 is the middle): each cell's healthy width measured on the atlas's own donors, a reading's distance from 1 counted in those widths, an off-centre middle flagged, not hidden. It sets, per cell type, the width used to judge a Met-A reading: a reading is called normal if |A - 1| <= k x width, with k the prediction interval for one new reading from n donors; readings are reported as widths from 1, and a middle more than 2 widths from 1 is flagged.

The instrument's job is the healthy height of each cell's identity sites and whether a type's level is physics or a quirk of IAM-A, so it needs this width to know, type by type, how far a reading can sit from 1 before it counts as off-centre rather than normal variation.
How it is obtained or computed

fields: Depth-matched expectation by exact hypergeometric subsampling (rarefaction) of sample and reference reads to a common depth

The Met-A expectation built with the sample and the reference read at a common depth m = min(sample reads, 20, every kept cell's reference reads) from their own reads: the sample thinned without replacement, the expectation drawn from each cell's own reference reads; A = sum hm / sum he, equal weights.

Sets m = min(sample reads, 20, every kept cell's reference reads); the sample is thinned without replacement to that depth, and the expectation is drawn from each cell's own reference reads (expected_H_mix_counts; for one cell, thin_H), giving A = sum hm / sum he with equal weights.

A thin reference (one library per donor half) cannot be taken as exact; reading both the sample and the reference at the same depth from their own reads removes the bias. The islands already worked this way.
How it is obtained or computed
Computed as exact hypergeometric draws (sampling without replacement) at the common depth m described above; this generalises the donor_pair and islands_counted rules, with nothing fitted.

record.law: IAM's Law, step 1d (The maintained hold (the slow write)): held/lost = (x/2)/(1 - (1 - e^-x)/x); sudden x -> 0 kept = lost; the cell at x = 2M: odds 21.45, E_hold 3.066 kT, phi = 0.1464 ~ ln M/M. Status: DERIVED (identity). IAM's Law, step 2 (The price): each nat costs at least k_BT held and k_BT spent; k_BT ln 2 per bit is the floor, paid at the receiving surface's own T. fields: Met-A = the sample's methylation disorder (Shannon entropy of the CpG's methylated fraction) over the disorder a healthy cell of the same composition shows at the same read depth. Three readings: sorted-cell Met-A (the library's own type's identity sites, against each healthy person of that type separately, averaged); Met-A for each cell in the mix (each found cell's identity sites against the atlas in the sample's shares); whole-sample Met-A (every IAM-Atlas v2.1 site, 790,761 in the test library, weighted |0.5 - e|, against the atlas in the sample's shares). 1 is healthy; above 1 the record is more disordered than healthy holds it, below 1 more ordered.

A cell that loses control of its record shows it first as disorder at sites a healthy cell holds firmly; comparing with the same type's healthy people at the same read depth removes the counting noise that depth alone would add, so a shallow library does not look disordered.

IAM's Law in the cell (link 1d, the maintained hold): the healthy level at held sites is set by the same hold as IAM-A's floor, 1/(1 + e^M) with M = 20.94; the gauge's floor and ceiling are derived (M1). Met-A reads the record's disorder; IAM-A reads its losses on held molecules: two views of the same hold.

The sample's level and read count at each site (from its molecules). The IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458, Zenodo record): each type's healthy level per person, the sealed donor halves and two noise maps (map 1 donor halves, map 2 read halves); the identity-site rule (healthy spread <= 0.05; mean 0.75-0.95 or 0.05-0.25; at most 3,000 per side). The Deconvolver's shares for the mix readings, through Met-A's tare on sorted samples.

Held-out pass 8 (each of 137 atlas libraries read against its other donor half): whole sample 0.990 +/- 0.177; sorted cell and own cell in the mix measured (bucket bands8/held_out_pass8.csv). Never-used healthy libraries (31 atlas types): whole sample 0.938 before the tare, 1.016 with it; sorted cell 1.004. Planted mixtures: whole sample within 0.03 of 1 for planted fractions >= 0.15.

Expected disorder computed at the sample's own read count at each site (counting noise modelled: exact draws, the counted expectation of 2026-11-20, common depth at most 20). Healthy bars by the 2026-11-07 rule: 1 is the middle; each type's width from its held-out person-to-person spread, Student's t coverage for few libraries (GUM). The 0.95-1.05 range in the code is a holdover from the old class method and is being retired.

records.name: Met-A on sequencing: its three readings, its healthy reference and how it is defended
questions: Why entropy and not just the methylation level?
Two samples can have the same average level while one is ordered (every molecule alike) and the other disordered (molecules disagree); a cell losing control of its record shows the disorder first.
field description; Met-A record
Doesn't low read depth make a sample look disordered?
It would, so the healthy expectation is computed at the sample's own read count at each site: counting noise is in the expectation, not mistaken for disorder.
counted expectation (2026-11-20); held-out passes
Why three readings?

They answer different questions: has this cell type's identity record moved (sorted cell), which cell in a mixture moved (each cell), has the sample as a whole departed (whole sample). They use different sites and expectations, so they can differ on one library.
METAA_SEQ_READINGS (SOP and Decoder)
How is Met-A's healthy range set?
Not by a fixed number: 1 is the middle and each type's width is its held-out person-to-person spread with Student's t coverage (GUM). The bars from the held-out pass with the tare are being measured.
the 2026-11-07 rule; pass 8 and pass 9
Were the healthy references ever used to test themselves?
No: every atlas library is read against the other, sealed donor half, and never-used libraries are kept for the out-of-sample check.
sealed donor halves; never-used GSE186458 libraries

fields: SORTED (isolated, purified) sequenced samples only; in whole blood, plasma and tissue Met-A keeps the Deconvolver's shares and no cell is assumed absent. Inside Met-A's healthy expectation: the Deconvolver's largest share is the main cell; a share in the main cell's tissue family (stage_0_intake.lineage_group) counts as the main cell; a cell in another family keeps its share only at or above SPILL_FLOOR = 0.05; megakaryocytes are left out (identification only); the rest is renormalized. The sorted label is recorded but never used: when it names a different type, the Deconvolver's call is used and the disagreement is flagged (tested: reading against the label's type moved Met-A away from 1). The Deconvolver, its reported shares, IAM-A in the mix and the mixture check are unchanged.

On healthy pure libraries the Deconvolver names the main cell but gives a few per cent to related references in the same tissue family (colon epithelium -> colon enteroendocrine 0.190; heart fibroblasts -> smooth muscle 0.238; tongue base -> tonsil palatine 0.305). Taken as real cells, those shares make Met-A's expected disorder too high at the sites where those references differ, so a healthy sample read low: median whole-sample Met-A 0.938 on 31 never-used healthy libraries (sorted-cell Met-A on the same libraries 1.004). In grid terms: the meter and relay are right; the setpoint was built with phantom load added in.

Not a step of IAM's Law: a calibration of the reference that Met-A (the disorder of the record against its healthy expectation) is read against. Met-A's expectation is the entropy of the atlas mixed in the sample's shares; entropy is steep near 0 and 1, so a few per cent of a related type at a firmly held site raises the expected disorder much more than it changes the level (the reason small shares bias Met-A, recorded 2026-11-21).

(1) The Deconvolver's shares for the sample (Stage D21, deconv_reference_v1, 5,699 marker CpGs, 57 types). (2) The chain's tissue families (stage_0_intake.lineage_group, the same map the mixture check uses). (3) SPILL_FLOOR from spill25.csv: every non-main share on 25 pure healthy libraries of atlas types (GSE186458, never used to build the atlas; real types from each GEO file name, lib49_real_types.csv).

Spill on the 25 pure libraries: 326 non-main shares, median 0.006, 0.95 quantile 0.053, largest 0.305; 15 of 19 shares of 0.05 or more stay in the main cell's family. Whole-sample Met-A on the 31 never-used atlas-type libraries: median 0.938 with the Deconvolver's shares, 1.016 with the rule; correlation with sorted-cell Met-A 0.18 -> 0.51; 27 of 31 within the GUM bar. Outside: GSM5652341 Prostate-Epithelial 0.865 (z -6.27, k 4.3); GSM5652237 Liver-Hepatocytes 1.200 (z 2.33, k 2.0); GSM5652330 Tongue_base-Epithelial 1.166 (z 4.84, k 4.3); GSM5652261 Kidney-Glomerular-Podocytes 1.208 (z 5.30, k 4.3).

Bar by the GUM (JCGM 100:2008): u = each cell type's person-to-person standard deviation of held-out sorted-cell Met-A (held-out pass 8, each atlas library read against the other donor half), pooled 0.086 over 137 libraries where a type has fewer than 3; coverage factor Student's t at n - 1 degrees of freedom for the type's library count (k = 4.30 for 3 libraries; Student 1908), 2 for large n. Not yet in u (both widen the bar): each read's counting noise and the shares' own uncertainty. The floor is the 0.95 quantile of measured spill, set from spill25.csv before the run; the prediction was written first.

Inject and recover (jobs/plant_mix.py: two healthy libraries' molecules mixed at known fractions, seeded binomial thinning): cardiomyocyte GSM5652214 + hepatocyte GSM5652236, and oligodendrocytes GSM5652222 + pancreatic acinar GSM5652246, at 0/0.05/0.10/0.15/0.20/0.30/0.50, read through the one button. With the rule, pair 1 reads 0.984/1.055/0.969/0.993/0.994/0.998/1.015 and pair 2 1.016/1.098/1.019/1.015/1.005/0.999/0.988 (with the Deconvolver's shares: 0.894/0.897/0.922/0.956/0.973/0.996/0.996 and 0.952/0.969/0.977/0.980/0.974/0.974/0.976). The chain's tare_shares is checked to give exactly the tested mixes (a chain update smoke). Known-answer run after the edit: 62 of 1,216 numbers moved, all in Met-A's mix route; whole-sample Met-A 0.894 -> 0.984 on the test library, as predicted.

(1) A real admixture below 0.05 from another family reads as pure (the detection limit; the 5 % plantings read 1.055 and 1.098). (2) A real mixture inside one family (e.g. fibroblasts with smooth muscle) is read as the main cell: its size is not yet measured (owed: a planted within-family mixture). (3) A large false share from another family stays (cortex neuron GSM5652232: striated muscle 0.244 kept, Met-A 0.861). (4) The within-family name can be wrong (podocytes called kidney tubular epithelium) while the family is right: Met-A's mix is unaffected, the name is. (5) Same laboratory as the atlas; a second laboratory's healthy libraries are owed. (6) Sequencing only; arrays untested. (7) The tissue families are broad (all 26 epithelia are one family, hepatocytes and pancreatic acinar included): stromal (6): adipocytes, cardiomyocyte, colon fibroblasts, heart fibroblasts, smooth muscle, striated muscle; endothelial (6): aorta endothelium, kidney glomerular endothelium, kidney tubular endothelium, lung alveolar endothelium, pancreas endothelium, vascular saphenous endothelium; B cells (2): b cells, memory b cells; epithelial (26): bladder epithelium, breast basal epithelium, breast luminal epithelium, colon enteroendocrine, colon epithelium, endometrium epithelium, fallopien tubes epithelium, gastric antrum epithelium, gastric body epithelium, gastric fundus epithelium, hepatocyte, kidney glomerular epithelium, kidney tubular epithelium, lung alveolar epithelium, lung bronchus epithelium, pancreatic acinar, pancreatic alpha, pancreatic beta, pancreatic delta, pancreatic duct, prostate epithelium, small intestine epithelium, thyroid epithelium, tongue epithelium, tonsil palatine epithelium, tonsil pharyngeal epithelium; T cells (8): cd4 t cells, cd8 t cells, effector memory cd8 t cells, naive cd4 t cells, naive cd8 t cells, t central memory cd4, t effector cell cd8, t effector memory cd4; monocytes and macrophages (4): colon macrophages, lung alveolar macrophages, lung interstitial macrophages, monocytes; neural (2): cortical neurons, oligodendrocytes; erythrocyte progenitors (1): erythrocyte progenitors; granulocytes (1): granulocytes; nk cells (1): nk cells. (9) The test sets' 'real types' are GEO file names: the best available truth, still labels. (5) On a sorted sample the tare's mix also sets which cells 'Met-A for each cell in the mix' and the globe's per-cell layer read: the cells it leaves out are not read individually (on the test library they were spill at 2-3 % that read the main cell's DNA). records.name: Met-A's tare on sequencing: the Deconvolver's spill inside a tissue family
questions: Why not fix the Deconvolver instead?

Its job is identification, and it names the main cell correctly; its shares are still reported unchanged. The bias comes only from how Met-A used near-miss shares between related references, so the correction sits in Met-A's tare.
tare_rule_judged.csv
Was the 0.05 floor tuned to make Met-A read 1?
No. It is the 0.95 quantile (0.053) of every non-main share measured on 25 pure healthy libraries (spill25.csv), set before the run; the prediction was written in the design sheet before any read.
spill25.csv; the design sheet written before the run
Doesn't this hide real mixtures?

Not across families at 10 % or more: planted mixtures keep their mix and read 0.969-1.019. Below 0.05 a cross-family admixture reads as pure (detection limit). Inside one family a real mixture is read as the main cell; its effect is not yet measured and is owed.
plantmix_14.csv; known-answer section
Why is sorted-cell Met-A the comparison?

It reads only the type's identity sites against each healthy donor separately, so it does not depend on the shares. It is the independent route; the rule moved whole-sample Met-A toward it (correlation 0.18 -> 0.51).
frag_rule49.csv;
How were the pass/fail bars set?
By the GUM (JCGM 100:2008): each type's person-to-person standard deviation from held-out readings, with Student's t coverage for small library counts. No chosen number.
tare_rule_judged.csv (sigma, n_libs, k, z)
Which libraries, and were they used to build the atlas?
49 sorted GSE186458 libraries never used to build the IAM Sequencing Atlas; real types from each GEO file name; 31 are atlas types and are the test set.
lib49_real_types.csv;
Why do four libraries fall outside?

GSM5652341 Prostate-Epithelial 0.865 (z -6.27, k 4.3); GSM5652237 Liver-Hepatocytes 1.200 (z 2.33, k 2.0); GSM5652330 Tongue_base-Epithelial 1.166 (z 4.84, k 4.3); GSM5652261 Kidney-Glomerular-Podocytes 1.208 (z 5.30, k 4.3). Two are read against a different site or the wrong type within the family, one is the prostate reference (thin donors), one matches its own sorted-cell reading.
tare_rule_judged.csv
Is this independent of the atlas's own laboratory?
Not yet: every library here comes from the atlas's laboratory. A second laboratory's healthy libraries (already aligned cord-blood B cells and CD4 T cells) are the owed independent check.
owed list
Does it change array readings?
No. It applies only to sorted sequenced samples; arrays are untested and unchanged.
a chain update (a._seqv)
Can it be rebuilt from public data?
Yes: the libraries are public (GEO GSE186458), the chain is public, and the tables, job scripts and seeds are in the development record.

Isn't trusting the sorted label what went wrong before?

Yes, and it was tested here too. A step that let a sorted label name the main cell inside its family was tried on three podocyte libraries: read against the label's type, Met-A moved away from 1 (1.208 -> 1.271, 1.016 -> 1.092), so the molecules sided with the Deconvolver. The label is never used; a disagreeing label is only flagged.
Met-A tare record, limit 8; the podocyte test of 2026-11-21
Why only sorted samples?

Because only there is one cell type expected; in whole blood, plasma and tissue a few per cent of any cell may be real (e.g. liver DNA in plasma), so dropping small shares there would assume absence. The rule was tested only on sorted libraries.
